data.name: My Little Kitties
data.detailed_description:
A heart-warming comedy of living with adorable kittens!

Bakeneko -Cats who shapeshift utilizing spiritual energy, due to being soul-bound to our world. The ghost of cats. (From World Research Company's, "The Complete Works of Orient Ghosts")

But, are bakenekos that scary...?
Losing his parents to a traffic accident, a boy lived his daily life in solitude until he began to take care of the stray kitten "Nuri"!
However, this kitten possessed strange powers similar to that of the bakeneko.
If that weren't enough, he met "Yura," who manages the existence of souls, and "Sora" from out of the blue.
With a strange twist of fate, the boy will begin raising two children...
And from that day, the boy will start his hectic child raising life.

Would you care to watch over the boy's daily life with his new heartwarming family?

Features:
  • Heroines are fully voiced.
  • Download their voices as ringtones to feel closer to the story.
  • Get along with Nuri and rest of the cast with assortments of mini games.

Voice Cast:
  • Nuri (CV: Kido Ibuki)
  • Sora (CV: Sakura Ayane)
  • Yura (CV: Uchida Maaya)

reviews.review:
My Little Kitties is a visual novel developed by COSEN and published by Sekai Project that embraces a simple but endearing premise: what if the stray kittens you welcomed into your home were actually mystical beings capable of becoming human? Drawing inspiration from Japanese folklore, the game introduces players to a world where bakeneko quietly coexist alongside ordinary people. Rather than turning this concept into an action-driven fantasy, the developers focus on the emotional possibilities of the idea, crafting a story that values personal connections and everyday moments above spectacle.

The narrative follows a young protagonist whose life becomes increasingly intertwined with several unusual cats after a chance encounter. As the story unfolds, each of these companions reveals her own personality, motivations, and emotional baggage. The game's description emphasizes warmth and comedy, and it delivers both consistently. Much of the appeal comes from watching the cast navigate mundane situations with a supernatural twist, resulting in plenty of lighthearted exchanges. At the same time, the writing gradually introduces more meaningful themes surrounding loneliness, acceptance, and the importance of finding a place where one belongs. This balance keeps the story from becoming overly sentimental while giving it enough emotional depth to stand apart from more generic visual novels.

One of the game's greatest strengths is its cast. Each character contributes something unique to the experience, ensuring that interactions remain engaging throughout the campaign. The chemistry between the protagonist and his feline companions feels natural, making it easy to become invested in their relationships. While the plot itself remains relatively modest in scope, the emphasis on character development proves to be the right decision. Players who enjoy visual novels primarily for their writing and interpersonal dynamics will find plenty to appreciate here. The game succeeds by making small moments matter, whether it is a comedic misunderstanding, a heartfelt conversation, or a quiet scene shared between characters.

Visually, My Little Kitties presents itself with charming anime-inspired artwork that complements its tone. Character portraits are expressive, and the softer color palette helps reinforce the game's comfortable atmosphere. The backgrounds, while not particularly elaborate, effectively establish the domestic setting that serves as the backdrop for much of the story. Voice performances add an extra layer of personality, helping each heroine feel distinct and memorable. Although the production values reflect its era and budget, the presentation remains cohesive and accomplishes exactly what it sets out to do.

The game's pacing is intentionally relaxed, which can be both a strength and a limitation. Players expecting branching mechanics or substantial gameplay systems may be disappointed, as My Little Kitties remains firmly rooted in the traditional visual novel format. Reading occupies the majority of the experience, and the title asks its audience to appreciate character interactions over interactivity. Fortunately, the writing generally maintains enough momentum to justify its slower approach. The folklore elements are also integrated thoughtfully, introducing players to the concept of bakeneko without requiring prior knowledge of Japanese mythology. This accessibility allows the game to appeal to both longtime visual novel enthusiasts and newcomers interested in supernatural slice-of-life stories.

Despite being released in 2016, My Little Kitties retains much of its charm today. Its greatest accomplishment is the sincerity with which it tells its story. It never attempts to be larger than it needs to be, instead focusing on delivering a heartfelt experience centered on companionship and family. While its limited gameplay and measured pacing may not resonate with everyone, those willing to embrace its quieter moments will discover a pleasant and memorable visual novel that understands the value of emotional storytelling.

Rating: 7/10
